question:
A 54-year-old woman presents to the office with a 2-week history of recurrent low back pain. She
mentions that she recently helped her friend move into a new apartment. Her medical history is
remarkable for type 2 diabetes mellitus controlled with metformin. Examination reveals a deep sacral
sulcus on the left and a posterior inferior lateral angle (ILA) on the right; there is no tenderness on
palpation. Lumbosacral spring test is positive. L5 is flexed, rotated left, and sidebent left. The patient
consents to receiving osteopathic manipulative treatment. Treatment with muscle energy involves
positioning the patient in the Answer Choices: (A) right lateral recumbent position with trunk rotation (B)
prone position with lumbar flexion (C) left lateral Sims position with face down (D) prone position with
lumbar extension (E) left lateral recumbent position with face down and hip flexion (F) left lateral
recumbent position with face up (G) supine position with hip flexion (H) seated position with forward

flexion (I) right lateral Sims position with face down (J) right lateral recumbent position with face up
 A. right lateral Sims position with face down
B. prone position with lumbar extension
C. right lateral recumbent position with trunk rotation
D. seated position with forward flexion
E. left lateral Sims position with face down
F. prone position with lumbar flexion
G. left lateral recumbent position with face down and hip flexion
H. left lateral recumbent position with face up
I. supine position with hip flexion
J. right lateral recumbent position with face up
